mfg1-electrical-l085.title: Connect specific hazards and signs to work
mfg1-electrical-l085.objective: Relate hazards involving safety devices, transport, solvents and disaster signs to specific actions.

paragraphs.title: Safety devices and people nearby
paragraphs.text: Fixing one button of a two-hand machine frees a hand to enter the danger area. Distinguish removed guards, disabled sensors and third parties approaching an open rear side. Locate emergency stops before work; their presence does not justify omitting guards.

paragraphs.title: Maintain visibility and clear routes
paragraphs.text: Loads blocking forward vision, open drains, stair cables and projections can cause collisions or falls. If a load hides your feet on stairs, do not proceed blindly; confirm an approved handling method. For solvent work, treat stopped ventilation, open containers and wet floors as separate hazards.

paragraphs.title: Identify the sign’s subject
paragraphs.text: No running, no mobile phones and no electronic devices are prohibition signs. Tsunami hazard zones differ from tsunami evacuation sites; rockfall and landslide warnings identify disaster types. Do not interchange flame, corrosion, health-hazard, aquatic-hazard and irritation information; match product identification to the SDS. A wide-area evacuation site may provide a broad space for refuge from major fires.

terms.meaning: An operating method requiring both hands at the controls.

mfg1-electrical-l085.activity:
30-minute study target: reading10 minutes, organizing examples8, writing9, reflection3.
For a fixed start button and transport with blocked forward vision, make four columns: hazard source, human action, likely injury and measures needing approval.
safety: For equipment operation, measurement, machining or setting changes, verify qualifications, training, responsibility limits and approved procedures.
mfg1-electrical-l085.summary: In “Connect specific hazards and signs to work”, compare construction, application and applicability conditions rather than names alone.

mfg1-electrical-l086.title: Read drawing requirements for paper, lines and lettering
mfg1-electrical-l086.objective: Distinguish paper dimensions, line types and widths, lettering and dimension annotations.

paragraphs.title: Paper and borders
paragraphs.text: A0 is841×1189 mm;A1 594×841;A2 420×594;A3 297×420;A4 210×297. Textbook border examples use10 mm margins forA4–A2 and20 mm forA1 and larger. Check the adopted format and binding margin on the drawing; do not treat the paper edge itself as a dimensional reference.

paragraphs.title: Widths and line types
paragraphs.text: The textbook’s basic thin/thick ratio is1:2, with examples0.18/0.35,0.25/0.5,0.35/0.7 and0.5/1.0 mm. Keep widths consistent for the same purpose in a drawing. Datum and pitch lines use chain lines; phantom lines for movement ranges may use double-chain lines; break boundaries use wavy or zigzag lines. Cutting-plane indications differ from section hatching.

paragraphs.title: Legible annotation
paragraphs.text: Example lettering heights are2.5,3.5,5,7 and10 mm. Avoid crossing dimension lines and duplicate dimensions; show finished sizes clearly. Arc length, chord length and central angle differ. Textbook process annotationsM andL indicate milling and turning and are read alongsideRa values. Check symbol editions and drawing legends.

terms.meaning: A line indicating adjacent parts, motion ranges or similar features.

mfg1-electrical-l086.activity:
30-minute study target: reading10 minutes, organizing examples8, writing9, reflection3.
Calculate the paper size obtained by halvingA2. Explain outlines, phantom lines, cutting planes and hatching by purpose. Explain why machining must wait when duplicate dimensions disagree.
safety: For equipment operation, measurement, machining or setting changes, verify qualifications, training, responsibility limits and approved procedures.

mfg1-electrical-l087.title: Check electrical symbols against terminals and operation
mfg1-electrical-l087.objective: Match electrical symbols to equipment terminals, actuation and return conditions.

paragraphs.title: Symbol shape and function
paragraphs.text: Match resistor, variable-resistor, capacitor and coil symbols to their functions. For diodes,LEDs and photodiodes, checkA/K and whether light arrows are present and their direction. A pnp transistor hasB/C/E; its three connections are not interchangeable. A symbol is not a photograph of actual shape or terminal order.

paragraphs.title: Actuation and return
paragraphs.text: Distinguish automatic return of pushbuttons or alarm switches from maintained emergency-stop actuation and manual release. Limit-switch symbols may indicate make, break or positive opening. Proximity and mechanical position switches also use different sensing principles. Similar names do not replace symbol/contact-behavior checks.

paragraphs.title: Equipment identifiers and references
paragraphs.text: The textbook usesR for relays,MC for contactors,THR for thermal relays,BS for pushbuttons andL for lamps. Other diagrams may use different identifiers, so follow the legend. Distinguish ammetersA, fuses, circuit breakers and indicator lamps; follow functional relationships left-to-right horizontally or top-to-bottom vertically. Match coils and contacts by equipment number and location reference.

terms.meaning: Returning to the original state when operation is released.

mfg1-electrical-l087.activity:
30-minute study target: reading10 minutes, organizing examples8, writing9, reflection3.
On an independently prepared symbol diagram, identify a resistor, capacitor, coil, diode,LED, photodiode,a-contact,b-contact, ammeter and fuse and explain each function. Do not reproduce the sourcePDF figures; compare the legend.
safety: For equipment operation, measurement, machining or setting changes, verify qualifications, training, responsibility limits and approved procedures.
mfg1-electrical-l087.summary: In “Check electrical symbols against terminals and operation”, compare construction, application and applicability conditions rather than names alone.

mfg1-electrical-l088.title: Use conditional comparisons of materials and insulation
mfg1-electrical-l088.objective: Interpret conductor, magnetic-material and insulation comparison values with their conditions.

paragraphs.title: Conductor comparison conditions
paragraphs.text: The textbook compares aluminum conductivity at about60% of annealed copper and density at about one third. Low mass and good conduction are different advantages. Its20°C resistivity values are1/58 for annealed copper,1/55 for hard copper and1/35 for aluminum, used inΩ·mm²/m with area accounted for. Retain material and temperature assumptions; do not generalize to every alloy.

paragraphs.title: Magnetic and resistance materials
paragraphs.text: Nichrome and similar resistance materials exploit heating. Some materials minimize resistance changes with temperature; low resistance is not best for every use. Permeability and saturation flux density matter for cores; remanence and coercivity matter for permanent magnets. Compare ferrite and alnico by application requirements rather than one generic “magnetic strength.”

paragraphs.title: Insulation structure and temperature
paragraphs.text: PET is thermoplastic, withMylar as an example name; phenolic and epoxy are thermosetting examples. Kraft paper and pressboard are insulation-paper examples; mica and ceramics are inorganic examples. The textbook explains temperature-rise limits by subtracting an ambient40°C from a maximum temperature, but this is not a universal product-use-limit formula. Also check temperature and reference water for specific-gravity comparisons.

terms.meaning: A property related to resistance to changing a magnetized state.

mfg1-electrical-l088.activity:
30-minute study target: reading10 minutes, organizing examples8, writing9, reflection3.
Compare resistivities of annealed copper and aluminum at equal length and area, separately from weight-saving benefits. Distinguish the textbook calculation155°C minus40°C for classF from checking a real product’s ambient-temperature limits.
safety: For equipment operation, measurement, machining or setting changes, verify qualifications, training, responsibility limits and approved procedures.
mfg1-electrical-l088.summary: In “Use conditional comparisons of materials and insulation”, compare construction, application and applicability conditions rather than names alone.

mfg1-electrical-l089.title: Match fastener shapes to tools
mfg1-electrical-l089.objective: Compare screw heads, nuts, washers and tool compatibility with the drawing.

paragraphs.title: Tools turning the nut
paragraphs.text: A box driver, also called a nut driver, turns small nuts. Open-end and ring spanners must match the hex across-flats dimension; adjust an adjustable wrench without clearance. Check load direction against the movable-jaw construction and instructions, avoiding force that opens its jaws.

paragraphs.title: Heads and washers
paragraphs.text: Machine screws include pan, countersunk and raised-countersunk heads; slotted and cross recesses require different tool fits. Washer-assembled screws are also calledSEMS screws. Flat washers spread load over the contact area and have specified positions, including metal/nonmetal combinations. Spring washers do not guarantee against loosening under every condition.

paragraphs.title: Compare actual parts and drawings
paragraphs.text: Textbook mounting examples include holding the equipment-side screw head while tightening its nut, and fastening into tapped holes with machine screws. Different materials or receiving threads may change the assembly. Plastic/rubber washers and locking nuts also exist; matching photographs do not authorize substitution. Check part number, orientation, count and torque.

terms.meaning: A screw supplied with washers incorporated.

mfg1-electrical-l089.activity:
30-minute study target: reading10 minutes, organizing examples8, writing9, reflection3.
Group the tools for hex-socket bolts, hex nuts and cross-recess screws. Write checks needed before tightening when a specified flat washer for a nonmetal plate is missing.
safety: For equipment operation, measurement, machining or setting changes, verify qualifications, training, responsibility limits and approved procedures.

mfg1-electrical-l090.title: Check cutting-tool sequence and geometry to retain
mfg1-electrical-l090.objective: Distinguish drilling and threading stages, tools and feed conditions before deciding.

paragraphs.title: Holes and threads are separate operations
paragraphs.text: A textbook handworking example for a large square hole places spaced small holes inside the outline, cuts between them and files the remaining allowance. Do not cross the marked line; control workholding and sharp edges. General hole/chamfer examples are not universal machining instructions; follow part drawings and material.

paragraphs.title: Tap and cutting-edge designs
paragraphs.text: Hand-tap sets may use first, intermediate and finishing taps in order. Choose for through/blind conditions and tool design; do not force an identical backing-off amount on every design. Drill flutes help remove chips. The textbook’s118° tip angle is representative, not universal for all materials. Distinguish brazed-tip and indexable turning tools.

paragraphs.title: Machine parts and feed
paragraphs.text: Lathes include headstock, chuck, toolpost, tailstock and feed mechanisms, combining workpiece rotation and tool feed. Milling uses relative motion between spindle tools and the table. Backlash is play affecting position after reversal. Check removal/compensation mechanisms and specifications; identical graduations do not always mean identical actual positions.

terms.meaning: Material left to be removed during finishing.

mfg1-electrical-l090.activity:
30-minute study target: reading10 minutes, organizing examples8, writing9, reflection3.
Show the inside/outside of the marked line and retained allowance for a square hole. If position does not follow immediately after reversing feed, separate observations from items to verify.
safety: For equipment operation, measurement, machining or setting changes, verify qualifications, training, responsibility limits and approved procedures.

mfg1-electrical-l091.title: Distinguish measurement principles from scale resolution
mfg1-electrical-l091.objective: Separate resolution from accuracy and explain temperature, magnetic-flux and capacitance measurement principles.

paragraphs.title: Mechanism and minimum reading
paragraphs.text: The textbook micrometer advances0.5 mm per turn with50 thimble divisions, giving0.01 mm per division. Display resolution and accuracy differ. Some dial indicators read0.001 mm, but this is not every model; also check range, contact and management condition.

paragraphs.title: Converting temperature and flux density
paragraphs.text: Thermocouples use thermoelectric voltage associated with temperature differences between junctions of two metals. The textbook’s typeK range is only an example; diameter, sheath, atmosphere and instrument change usable limits. In aHall element, a field perpendicular to current produces voltage perpendicular to both, a principle used in gaussmeters.

paragraphs.title: Inferring other quantities electrically
paragraphs.text: LCR auto-balancing bridges use voltage, current and phase to obtain component values. Capacitance is the capacity to store charge between conductors; changes can detect thickness, displacement or liquid level. Distinguish the target quantity and electrical conversion; a capacitance change alone does not establish one unique cause.

terms.meaning: Voltage associated with a temperature difference between junctions.

mfg1-electrical-l091.activity:
30-minute study target: reading10 minutes, organizing examples8, writing9, reflection3.
Calculate0.5 mm per turn divided by50, and explain resolution versus accuracy. Map input and output quantities of thermocouples,Hall elements and capacitive displacement sensing with arrows.
safety: For equipment operation, measurement, machining or setting changes, verify qualifications, training, responsibility limits and approved procedures.
mfg1-electrical-l091.summary: In “Distinguish measurement principles from scale resolution”, compare construction, application and applicability conditions rather than names alone.
